functional.text: Starting from seed URLs, crawl the web: fetch HTML pages, store them, extract links and add new URLs to the frontier.
Avoid duplicate work: each URL is fetched once per cycle; pages whose content duplicates an earlier page are not stored or indexed twice.
Recrawl pages to keep them fresh, more often for pages that change often.
Expose stored pages to the indexing team for 6 months.

non_functional.text: Polite: at most 1 request/s per host and obey robots.txt (disallow rules, crawl-delay).
Throughput: 2B pages per month, scaling horizontally by adding fetchers.
Robust against crawler traps, slow servers and malformed HTML; no lost work when a machine dies.

assumptions.text: ~100 KB per HTML page; ~1/3 of fetched pages are copies or near-copies.

out_of_scope.text: Images/video, JavaScript rendering, building the search index itself.

api.notes: Internal control API; also used to force a recrawl.
Lets operators slow down or block a host after a complaint.

data.name: url_meta
data.fields: url_hash (PK), url, host, priority, last_fetched, next_fetch_at, content_hash, status, depth
data.why: Billions of rows, point lookups and updates by url_hash; drives recrawl (next_fetch_at).

data.name: frontier
data.fields: front queues by priority → back queues per host; heap of (host, ready_at)
data.why: Ordering and politeness live in the queue structure; persisted to disk with checkpoints.

data.name: pages
data.fields: blob key url_hash/fetch_time → compressed HTML + response headers, batched into large files
data.why: Write-once, read in bulk by indexing: ~1.2 PB raw for 6 months.

deep_dives.title: Politeness at scale

options.name: one global FIFO
options.cons: links cluster by site: hundreds of fetchers hit one host at once

options.name: sleep between requests in each fetcher
options.cons: doesn't stop two fetchers hitting the same host

options.name: per-host back queues + ready-time heap
options.pros: one host is served by one fetcher at a time with an enforced delay
options.cons: more frontier machinery; must shard by host

deep_dives.choice: priority front queues feeding per-host back queues, released by a scheduler heap (host ready at t)
deep_dives.why: N1 and N2 together: politeness is enforced structurally, and throughput comes from crawling many hosts in parallel. robots.txt is fetched once per host and cached with its crawl-delay.

deep_dives.title: Detecting repeats

options.name: exact hash set of URLs in a DB
options.cons: ~1 TB of keys, a DB lookup per extracted link

options.name: Bloom filter over normalised URLs
options.pros: ~25 GB for 20B URLs at 1% false positives, in memory

deep_dives.choice: URL normalisation + Bloom filter for URLs; exact hash and SimHash fingerprints for content
deep_dives.why: F2: URL dedup prevents refetching (most of the volume); content dedup stops the 1/3 of copies being stored and indexed.

deep_dives.title: Priority and recrawl

options.name: BFS order, fixed revisit interval
options.cons: wastes budget on static pages, news goes stale

options.name: importance × staleness priority, adaptive interval
options.pros: budget follows value and change rate

deep_dives.choice: importance × staleness priority with adaptive revisit interval
deep_dives.why: F3: halve a URL's interval when its content hash changed, double it (to a cap) when it didn't; importance from link-based score and domain quality.

wrapup.bottlenecks: DNS resolution (local caching resolvers), the frontier (sharded by host hash so each host lives on one shard), the Bloom filter (partitioned by URL hash), and politeness itself: a few huge sites cap throughput, so breadth across hosts matters.
wrapup.failures: Fetcher crash: URLs are leased from the frontier and redelivered if not acked. Unhealthy host (5xx/timeouts): per-host exponential backoff. Traps: max depth, max URL length, page budget per host. Frontier shard loss: rebuilt from checkpoint + url_meta.
wrapup.monitoring: Pages/s fetched, error and timeout rate by host, frontier size and age, duplicate rate, robots.txt denials, DNS latency, bandwidth.
wrapup.scale: Add fetchers and frontier shards; place fetcher clusters in several regions close to the hosts they crawl (host-hash affinity).
wrapup.future: JavaScript rendering for dynamic sites, sitemaps and change feeds (push instead of poll), spam/link-farm detection.
